```{python}
import json
from html import escape

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site
from pdi.tech_value import catalogue as tvcat

# Bundle the table script into the page instead of loading it from a CDN.
init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

cpu, cpu_meta = site.load("tech-value", "residuals")
gpu, gpu_meta = site.load("tech-value", "gpu_residuals")
cpu_val, cpu_val_meta = site.load("tech-value", "residual_validation")
gpu_val, gpu_val_meta = site.load("tech-value", "gpu_residual_validation")
cat, cat_meta = site.load("tech-value", "catalogue")
PRICE = {} if cat.empty else {
    (r.kind, r.model_key): (float(r.price_usd), r.price_date)
    for r in cat.itertuples() if pd.notna(r.price_usd)
}
DATA = {"cpu": cpu, "gpu": gpu}
META = {"cpu": cpu_meta, "gpu": gpu_meta}
VAL = {"cpu": cpu_val, "gpu": gpu_val}
NOUN = {"cpu": "CPUs", "gpu": "GPUs"}
ONE = {"cpu": "processor", "gpu": "graphics card"}
MEASURE = {
    "cpu": "SPECrate 2017 Int base per socket",
    "gpu": "Calibrated SPEC GWPG score (site estimate)",
}
MODELS = {"ols": "OLS", "structural": "Structural L1", "nonlinear": "Nonlinear GBDT"}

# The pipeline's classifications, grouped into the four classes this page shows.
CLASS_OF = {
    "Above prediction across models": "above",
    "Below prediction across models": "below",
    "Model-sensitive (small-core)": "sensitive",
    "Model-sensitive (scaling regime)": "sensitive",
    "Model-sensitive (entry-level shaders)": "sensitive",
}
CLASSES = {
    "above": ("Above prediction across models", "Measured score above all three predictions.", "#18b47b"),
    "sensitive": ("Model-sensitive", "Above the straight-line model, much less so once scaling is allowed to bend.", "#f0b23e"),
    "near": ("Near prediction", "Within the models' usual error.", "#c4cad1"),
    "below": ("Below prediction across models", "A candidate for checking scaling, configuration or model limits.", "#d9707a"),
}
FONT = dict(family="Century Gothic, URW Gothic, Questrial, system-ui, sans-serif", color="#8391a1", size=12)
AXIS = dict(showgrid=False, showline=True, linecolor="#8391a1", ticks="outside", zeroline=False)
HOVER = dict(bgcolor="white", font_color="#14233a", font_family=FONT["family"])

for kind, df in DATA.items():
    if not df.empty:
        df["cls"] = df["consensus_verdict"].map(CLASS_OF).fillna("near")


def limited(r) -> bool:
    """Few disclosures, or every one from a single OEM: one configuration can carry the result."""
    return int(r["n_oems"]) <= 1 or int(r["n_results"]) < 4


def count(kind, cls):
    df = DATA[kind]
    return int((df["cls"] == cls).sum()) if not df.empty else 0


def day(ts):
    return str(ts)[:10] if ts else "not recorded"


def collected(meta):
    srcs = meta.get("sources") or []
    return day(srcs[0].get("retrieved_at")) if srcs else "not recorded"


def typical_error(kind):
    """Median absolute held-out error per model, over all ranked chips."""
    v = VAL[kind]
    if v.empty:
        return {}
    allrows = v[v["slice"] == "All"].set_index("model")
    return {m: float(r["median_abs_pct_error"]) for m, r in allrows.iterrows()}


ICON = {
    "chev": '<path d="M6 9l6 6 6-6"/>',
    "warn": '<path d="M12 3l10 18H2z"/><path d="M12 10v5M12 18v.5"/>',
}


def icon(name, cls=""):
    return f'<svg class="op-ico {cls}" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true">{ICON[name]}</svg>'


def raw(html):
    """Emit HTML as a raw block so pandoc does not re-parse it as markdown."""
    print(f"\n```{{=html}}\n{html}\n```\n")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
html = ""
for kind in ("cpu", "gpu"):
    if DATA[kind].empty:
        continue
    cards = [
        (len(DATA[kind]), f"Ranked {NOUN[kind]}"),
        (count(kind, "above"), "Above prediction across models"),
        (count(kind, "sensitive"), "Model-sensitive"),
        (count(kind, "below"), "Below prediction across models"),
    ]
    body = "".join(f'<div class="op-kpi"><strong>{n:,}</strong><span>{label}</span></div>' for n, label in cards)
    html += f'<div class="op-kpis" data-kind="{kind}">{body}</div>'
html += '<p class="op-note">Agreement between models marks chips worth a closer look. It does not say why a chip differs.</p>'
for kind in ("cpu", "gpu"):
    if cat.empty:
        break
    c = cat[cat["kind"] == kind]
    counts = c["coverage_status"].value_counts()
    parts = " · ".join(f"{n:,} {s.lower()}" for s, n in counts.items())
    on_pages = c[c["on_value_ranking"] | c["on_fair_price"]]
    measured_there = int((on_pages["coverage_status"] == "Measured").sum())
    none_there = int((on_pages["coverage_status"] == "Results not found").sum())
    html += (f'<p class="op-note" data-kind="{kind}"><b>Coverage of {len(c):,} {NOUN[kind]} in the catalogue:</b> {parts}. '
             f'Of the {len(on_pages)} {NOUN[kind]} on Value ranking or Fair price, {measured_there} are measured here '
             f'and {none_there} have no SPEC result, which is common for consumer parts. '
             'See "Coverage of every product" below for each product and the reason.</p>')
raw(html)
```

```{python}
def log_ticks(lo, hi):
    vals = [m * 10 ** e for e in range(-2, 7) for m in (1, 2, 5)]
    return [v for v in vals if lo / 1.15 <= v <= hi * 1.15]


def main_chart(kind):
    """Measured against predicted, one set of points per model; the buttons switch models."""
    df = DATA[kind]
    y = df["measured_per_socket" if kind == "cpu" else "measured_score"]
    preds = [df[f"pred_{m}"] for m in MODELS]
    lo = float(min(y.min(), *(p.min() for p in preds)))
    hi = float(max(y.max(), *(p.max() for p in preds)))
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_scatter(x=[lo / 1.2, hi * 1.2], y=[lo / 1.2, hi * 1.2], mode="lines", hoverinfo="skip",
                    line=dict(color="#55606c", width=1.3), showlegend=False, name="equal")
    for key, label in MODELS.items():
        for cls in ("near", "sensitive", "below", "above"):
            part = df[df["cls"] == cls]
            if part.empty:
                continue
            ys = y[part.index]
            custom = np.stack([
                part["processor"], [CLASSES[cls][0]] * len(part),
                np.expm1(part[f"{key}_resid_log"]) * 100,
                part[f"pred_{key}_lo"], part[f"pred_{key}_hi"], part["n_results"], part["n_oems"],
            ], axis=-1)
            fig.add_scatter(
                x=part[f"pred_{key}"].tolist(), y=ys.tolist(), mode="markers", name=f"m:{key}:{cls}", visible=(key == "ols"),
                marker=dict(size=6 if cls == "near" else 8, color=CLASSES[cls][2],
                            opacity=0.7 if cls == "near" else 0.95, line=dict(width=0.6, color="rgba(255,255,255,0.8)")),
                customdata=custom.tolist(), showlegend=False,
                hovertemplate=(f"<b>%{{customdata[0]}}</b><br>%{{customdata[1]}}<br>Measured %{{y:,.1f}} · {label} %{{x:,.1f}}"
                               " (%{customdata[2]:+.1f}%)<br>80% range %{customdata[3]:,.1f} – %{customdata[4]:,.1f}"
                               "<br>%{customdata[5]} disclosures · %{customdata[6]} OEM(s)<extra></extra>"),
            )
    fig.add_scatter(x=[None], y=[None], mode="markers", name="selected", hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False,
                    marker=dict(size=17, color="rgba(24,180,123,0.2)", line=dict(width=2.4, color="#0f8f6c")))
    ticks = log_ticks(lo, hi)
    rng = [np.log10(lo / 1.15), np.log10(hi * 1.15)]
    fig.update_layout(
        height=460, font=FONT, margin=dict(t=10, r=10, b=54, l=74),
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        xaxis=dict(**AXIS, type="log", range=rng, tickvals=ticks, ticktext=[f"{t:,g}" for t in ticks],
                   title="Predicted by OLS (log scale)"),
        yaxis=dict(**AXIS, type="log", range=rng, tickvals=ticks, ticktext=[f"{t:,g}" for t in ticks],
                   title=f"Measured: {MEASURE[kind]}"),
        hoverlabel=HOVER, dragmode=False,
        annotations=[dict(x=0.98, y=0.04, xref="paper", yref="paper", showarrow=False, xanchor="right",
                          text="Line = measured equals predicted", font=dict(size=11, color="#8391a1"))],
    )
    fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True})


def legend(kind):
    items = "".join(
        f'<li><span class="op-dot" style="background:{c}"></span><span><b>{n}</b><small>{d}</small></span></li>'
        for n, d, c in CLASSES.values()
    )
    raw(f'<aside class="op-legend"><ul>{items}</ul><hr><small>Classes use all three models. '
        'The chart shows one model at a time.</small>'
        '<div class="op-callout">Above the line = measured score higher than predicted.</div></aside>')


def model_buttons(kind):
    err = typical_error(kind)
    btns = "".join(
        f'<button type="button" data-model="{k}" aria-pressed="{str(k == "ols").lower()}" '
        f'title="Typical held-out error {err.get(v, float("nan")):.1f}%">{v}</button>'
        for k, v in {"ols": "OLS", "structural": "Structural L1", "nonlinear": "Nonlinear GBDT"}.items()
    )
    raw(f'<div class="op-seg" role="group" aria-label="Prediction model">{btns}</div>')


def chip_rows(kind):
    df = DATA[kind]
    score = "measured_per_socket" if kind == "cpu" else "measured_score"
    rows = []
    for _, r in df.iterrows():
        preds = {}
        for key, col in (("ols", "ols"), ("structural", "structural"), ("nonlinear", "nonlinear")):
            preds[key] = dict(p=round(float(r[f"pred_{key}"]), 2),
                              lo=None if pd.isna(r[f"pred_{key}_lo"]) else round(float(r[f"pred_{key}_lo"]), 2),
                              hi=None if pd.isna(r[f"pred_{key}_hi"]) else round(float(r[f"pred_{key}_hi"]), 2),
                              r=round(float(np.expm1(r[f"{col}_resid_log"]) * 100), 1))
        facts = [
            ("Disclosures", int(r["n_results"])),
            ("OEMs", int(r["n_oems"])),
            ("Distinct systems", int(r["n_systems"])),
            ("Distinct configurations", int(r["n_configs"])),
        ]
        if kind == "cpu":
            facts += [("Sockets tested", r["sockets_tested"]),
                      ("Test dates", f'{day(r["first_test_date"])} to {day(r["last_test_date"])}'),
                      ("Config spread", f'{r["tuning_spread_pct"]:.1f} pts')]
            if pd.notna(r.get("peak_gain_pct")):
                facts.append(("Peak vs base compiler gain", f'{r["peak_gain_pct"]:+.1f}%'))
        else:
            facts += [("Suites", r["suites_tested"]), ("Released", int(r["generation"])),
                      ("Config spread", f'{r["tuning_spread_pct"]:.1f} pts'),
                      ("Workload specialization", f'{r["workload_specialization_pct"]:+.0f}%')]
        key = tvcat.key_of(kind, r["processor"])
        price, price_date = PRICE.get((kind, key), (None, None))
        if price:
            facts.append(("Retail price", f"${price:,.0f} ({price_date})"))
            facts.append((f"SPEC score per $100", f"{100 * float(r[score]) / price:,.1f}"))
        rows.append(dict(
            key=key, vendor=r["vendor"], group=r["family"], form=r.get("form_factor") or "",
            gen=None if pd.isna(r["generation"]) else int(r["generation"]),
            cores=float(r["cores_per_chip"]), price=price,
            name=r["processor"], cls=CLASSES[r["cls"]][0], y=round(float(r[score]), 2), preds=preds,
            spread=round(float(r["model_spread_pts"]), 1), oor=r["outside_training_range"] or "",
            limited=limited(r), facts=facts, url=r.get("disclosure_url") or "",
        ))
    return rows


def pick(kind):
    df = DATA[kind]
    rows = chip_rows(kind)
    above = df[df["cls"] == "above"]
    default = (above if len(above) else df).sort_values("nonlinear_resid_log").iloc[-1]["processor"]
    opts = "".join(f'<option{" selected" if d["name"] == default else ""}>{escape(d["name"])}</option>'
                   for d in sorted(rows, key=lambda d: d["name"]))
    err = typical_error(kind)
    err_txt = " · ".join(f"{m} {e:.1f}%" for m, e in err.items())
    raw(f"""<div class="op-pick" data-chips="{escape(json.dumps(rows), quote=True)}">
<div class="op-pick-head"><span class="op-pick-name" data-f="name"></span><span class="op-badge" data-f="cls"></span>
<label>Inspect a {ONE[kind]}<select aria-label="Inspect a {ONE[kind]}">{opts}</select></label></div>
<div class="op-pick-body">
<div><table class="op-preds"><thead><tr><th></th><th>Score</th><th>80% range</th><th>Residual</th></tr></thead><tbody data-f="preds"></tbody></table>
<div class="op-flag" data-f="flags"></div></div>
<div class="op-facts" data-f="facts"></div>
</div>
<div class="op-pick-foot">Typical held-out error: {escape(err_txt)}. Predicted scores are this site's estimates, not SPEC metrics.
<span data-f="link"></span></div>
</div>
<div class="tv-pick-panel" data-kind="{kind}" hidden></div>""")


def peers(kind):
    """Filters that narrow the main chart to comparable chips, with a count."""
    df = DATA[kind]

    def options(values, label):
        vals = sorted({str(v) for v in values if pd.notna(v) and str(v)})
        return f'<option value="">{label}: all</option>' + "".join(
            f'<option value="{escape(v)}">{escape(v)}</option>' for v in vals)

    years = sorted({int(v) for v in df["generation"].dropna()})
    yopts = lambda first: "".join(
        f'<option{" selected" if y == first else ""}>{y}</option>' for y in years)
    group_label = "Family" if kind == "cpu" else "Architecture"
    form = ("" if kind == "cpu" else
            f'<select data-peer="form" aria-label="Form factor">{options(df["form_factor"], "Form factor")}</select>')
    unit = "Cores" if kind == "cpu" else "Shaders"
    n_priced = sum(1 for p in df["processor"] if (kind, tvcat.key_of(kind, p)) in PRICE)
    raw(f"""<div class="op-peers" role="group" aria-label="Comparable {NOUN[kind]}">
<select data-peer="vendor" aria-label="Vendor">{options(df["vendor"], "Vendor")}</select>
<select data-peer="group" aria-label="{group_label}">{options(df["family"], group_label)}</select>{form}
<span class="op-peer-range">Released <select data-peer="gen0" aria-label="Released from">{yopts(years[0])}</select>
to <select data-peer="gen1" aria-label="Released to">{yopts(years[-1])}</select></span>
<span class="op-peer-range">{unit} <input data-peer="c0" type="number" min="0" placeholder="min" aria-label="{unit} at least">
<input data-peer="c1" type="number" min="0" placeholder="max" aria-label="{unit} at most"></span>
<span class="op-peer-range" title="Retail price from the Value ranking; known for {n_priced} of {len(df)}">Price $ <input data-peer="p0" type="number" min="0" placeholder="min" aria-label="Price at least">
<input data-peer="p1" type="number" min="0" placeholder="max" aria-label="Price at most"></span>
<button type="button" data-peer="reset" class="op-peer-reset">Reset</button>
<span class="op-peer-count" aria-live="polite"></span>
</div>""")


CMP_DEFAULT = {"cpu": ("amd ryzen 9 7950x", "intel core i9-13900k"),
               "gpu": ("nvidia rtx 4060", "amd radeon ai pro r9700")}


def compare(kind):
    """Two products side by side from the shared catalogue, ranked here or not."""
    head("Compare two products",
         f"Any two {NOUN[kind]} from the catalogue, with what each Tech Value page says about them. "
         "Blender and SPEC are separate benchmarks: each row compares like with like, and no row combines them.")
    if cat.empty:
        raw(site.empty_state(cat_meta, "Hardware catalogue"))
        return
    names = sorted(cat.loc[cat["kind"] == kind, "name"].dropna().unique())
    opts = "".join(f'<option value="{escape(n)}">' for n in names)
    a, b = CMP_DEFAULT[kind]
    raw(f"""<div class="op-cmp" data-kind="{kind}" data-a="{escape(a)}" data-b="{escape(b)}">
<div class="op-cmp-pick">
<label>First {ONE[kind]}<input type="search" list="op-cmp-list-{kind}" data-cmp="a" autocomplete="off" aria-label="First {ONE[kind]}"></label>
<label>Second {ONE[kind]}<input type="search" list="op-cmp-list-{kind}" data-cmp="b" autocomplete="off" aria-label="Second {ONE[kind]}"></label>
<datalist id="op-cmp-list-{kind}">{opts}</datalist>
</div>
<div class="op-cmp-wrap"><table class="op-cmp-table"><tbody data-cmp="body"><tr><td>Loading the catalogue…</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p class="op-cmp-sum" data-cmp="sum"></p>
<p class="op-foot">Prices are the dated lowest new listing used on Value ranking and Fair price. Blender points per dollar use
that same price. SPEC scores are {MEASURE[kind]}.</p>
</div>""")


def head(title, *ledes):
    raw(f"<h2>{title}</h2>" + "".join(f'<p class="op-lede">{t}</p>' for t in ledes))
```

```{python}
def agreement(kind):
    df = DATA[kind]
    o = np.expm1(df["ols_resid_log"]) * 100
    n = np.expm1(df["nonlinear_resid_log"]) * 100
    lim = max(60, float(np.ceil(max(o.abs().max(), n.abs().max()) / 20) * 20))
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_shape(type="rect", x0=0, y0=0, x1=lim, y1=lim, fillcolor="rgba(24,180,123,0.08)", line_width=0, layer="below")
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line=dict(color="#55606c", width=1))
    fig.add_vline(x=0, line=dict(color="#55606c", width=1))
    for cls in ("near", "sensitive", "below", "above"):
        m = (df["cls"] == cls).to_numpy()
        if not m.any():
            continue
        fig.add_scatter(x=o[m], y=n[m], mode="markers", showlegend=False,
                        marker=dict(size=6, color=CLASSES[cls][2], opacity=0.85),
                        customdata=df["processor"][m], hovertemplate="<b>%{customdata}</b><br>OLS %{x:+.1f}% · Nonlinear %{y:+.1f}%<extra></extra>")
    step = 20 if lim <= 100 else 40
    vals = list(range(-int(lim), int(lim) + 1, step))
    text = [f"{v:+d}%" if v else "0%" for v in vals]
    fig.update_layout(height=320, font=FONT, margin=dict(t=6, r=8, b=50, l=62),
                      paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
                      xaxis=dict(**AXIS, range=[-lim, lim], tickvals=vals, ticktext=text, title="Residual vs OLS (%)"),
                      yaxis=dict(**AXIS, range=[-lim, lim], tickvals=vals, ticktext=text, title="Residual vs nonlinear (%)"),
                      hoverlabel=HOVER, dragmode=False)
    fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True})


SHORT_GROUP = {
    "Intel oneAPI (LLVM)": "Intel oneAPI",
    "Oracle / Vendor Studio": "Oracle Studio",
    "SPECviewperf 15 (DX12 / Vulkan / OpenGL)": "SPECviewperf 15",
    "SPECviewperf 2020 (OpenGL / DX12)": "SPECviewperf 2020",
    "SPECviewperf 12.1 / 13 (Legacy OpenGL)": "SPECviewperf 12.1 / 13",
    "SPECworkstation (Full System + GPU)": "SPECworkstation",
    "SPECapc (Maya / Solidworks / Creo / 3ds Max)": "SPECapc",
}


def group_table(kind):
    df = DATA[kind]
    g = df.groupby("compiler_family").agg(
        chips=("processor", "size"), disclosures=("n_results", "sum"),
        spread=("tuning_spread_pct", "median"), configs=("n_configs", "median"),
        ols=("residual_pct", "median"), nonlinear=("gbdt_residual_pct", "median"),
    ).reset_index()
    return g.sort_values("disclosures", ascending=False)


def spread_chart(kind):
    g = group_table(kind).sort_values("disclosures")
    labels = [f"{SHORT_GROUP.get(f, f)} ({c})" for f, c in zip(g["compiler_family"], g["chips"])]
    fig = go.Figure()
    for y, v in zip(labels, g["spread"]):
        fig.add_shape(type="line", x0=0, x1=v, y0=y, y1=y, line=dict(color="#8391a1", width=1.5))
    fig.add_scatter(
        x=g["spread"], y=labels, mode="markers+text", text=[f"{v:.1f}" for v in g["spread"]],
        textposition="middle right", textfont=dict(color="#8391a1", size=12),
        marker=dict(size=12, color="#18b47b", line=dict(width=1, color="white")),
        customdata=np.stack([g["chips"], g["disclosures"], g["configs"]], axis=-1),
        hovertemplate="%{y}<br>Median spread %{x:.1f} pts<br>%{customdata[0]} chips · %{customdata[1]} disclosures"
                      "<br>Median %{customdata[2]} configurations per chip<extra></extra>",
        showlegend=False,
    )
    hi = float(np.ceil((g["spread"].max() * 1.25) / 5) * 5)
    fig.update_layout(
        height=max(240, 60 + 46 * len(g)), font=FONT, margin=dict(t=6, r=12, b=50, l=10),
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        xaxis=dict(**AXIS, range=[0, hi], title="Median spread across submitted configurations (pts)"),
        yaxis=dict(showgrid=False, showline=False, ticks="", automargin=True),
        hoverlabel=HOVER, dragmode=False,
    )
    fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True})


TIERS = {
    "cpu": ("l3_mb_per_core", [1.5, 3.0], ["Low L3", "Standard L3", "High L3"], "MB L3 per core"),
    "gpu": ("bandwidth_gbps", [200, 500], ["Low bandwidth", "Standard bandwidth", "High bandwidth"], "GB/s"),
}
TIER_COLORS = ["#d9707a", "#f0b23e", "#18b47b"]
SYMBOLS = {"Intel": "circle", "AMD": "diamond", "NVIDIA": "circle", "Other": "square"}


def scaling_chart(kind, metric):
    """metric 'unit': throughput per core or shader; 'total': measured score."""
    df = DATA[kind].dropna(subset=["cores_per_chip"]).copy()
    col, cuts, names, unit = TIERS[kind]
    df["tier"] = np.digitize(df[col].fillna(df[col].median()), cuts)
    if metric == "unit":
        df["yv"] = df["score_per_core"]
        ytitle = "Base score per core" if kind == "cpu" else "Score per 1,000 shaders"
    else:
        df["yv"] = df["measured_per_socket" if kind == "cpu" else "measured_score"]
        ytitle = "Base score per socket" if kind == "cpu" else "Calibrated score"
    fig = go.Figure()
    for t, name in enumerate(names):
        for vendor, symbol in SYMBOLS.items():
            part = df[(df["tier"] == t) & (df["vendor"] == vendor)]
            if part.empty:
                continue
            fig.add_scatter(
                x=part["cores_per_chip"], y=part["yv"], mode="markers", showlegend=False,
                marker=dict(size=7, symbol=symbol, color=TIER_COLORS[t], opacity=0.85, line=dict(width=0.6, color="rgba(255,255,255,0.8)")),
                customdata=np.stack([part["processor"], part[col], part["residual_pct"]], axis=-1),
                hovertemplate=f"<b>%{{customdata[0]}}</b><br>%{{x:,.0f}} {'cores' if kind == 'cpu' else 'shaders'} · "
                              f"%{{y:,.1f}}<br>%{{customdata[1]:.1f}} {unit} · OLS residual %{{customdata[2]:+.1f}}%<extra></extra>",
            )
    lo, hi = df["cores_per_chip"].min(), df["cores_per_chip"].max()
    xt = [2 ** e for e in range(0, 16) if lo / 1.5 <= 2 ** e <= hi * 1.5]
    if kind == "gpu":
        xt = [v for v in (500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000) if lo / 1.5 <= v <= hi * 1.5]
    yt = log_ticks(df["yv"].min(), df["yv"].max())
    fig.update_layout(
        height=320, font=FONT, margin=dict(t=6, r=10, b=50, l=64),
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        xaxis=dict(**AXIS, type="log", tickvals=xt, ticktext=[f"{v:,}" for v in xt],
                   title="Cores per chip (log scale)" if kind == "cpu" else "Shaders (log scale)"),
        yaxis=dict(**AXIS, type="log", tickvals=yt, ticktext=[f"{v:,g}" for v in yt], title=ytitle),
        hoverlabel=HOVER, dragmode=False,
    )
    fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True})


def scaling_buttons(kind):
    unit = "Per core" if kind == "cpu" else "Per 1,000 shaders"
    total = "Per socket" if kind == "cpu" else "Total"
    raw(f'<div class="op-seg" role="group" aria-label="Throughput measure"><button type="button" data-alt="unit" aria-pressed="true">{unit}</button>'
        f'<button type="button" data-alt="total" aria-pressed="false">{total}</button></div>')


def scaling_keys(kind):
    _, cuts, names, unit = TIERS[kind]
    bounds = [f"&lt; {cuts[0]:g} {unit}", f"{cuts[0]:g}–{cuts[1]:g} {unit}", f"&gt; {cuts[1]:g} {unit}"]
    tiers = "".join(f'<span><span class="op-dot" style="background:{c};margin:0"></span>{n} <small>({b})</small></span>'
                    for n, b, c in zip(names, bounds, TIER_COLORS))
    vendors = ["Intel", "AMD", "Other"] if kind == "cpu" else ["NVIDIA", "AMD"]
    shapes = "".join(f'<span><span class="op-shape {SYMBOLS[v]}"></span>{v}</span>' for v in vendors)
    raw(f'<div class="op-keys">{tiers}{shapes}</div>')


def accuracy(kind):
    v = VAL[kind]
    if v.empty:
        raw('<p class="op-lede">Model validation has not been exported yet.</p>')
        return
    a = v[v["slice"] == "All"]
    top = float(a["median_abs_pct_error"].max())
    rows = ""
    for _, r in a.iterrows():
        base = r["model"].startswith("Baseline")
        cov = "" if pd.isna(r["range_coverage_pct"]) else f'{r["range_coverage_pct"]:.0f}%'
        w = 100 * r["median_abs_pct_error"] / top if top else 0
        rows += (f'<tr class="{"op-base" if base else ""}"><td>{r["model"]}</td>'
                 f'<td><span class="op-bar" style="width:{w * 0.9:.0f}px"></span>{r["median_abs_pct_error"]:.1f}%</td>'
                 f'<td>{cov}</td><td>{int(r["n_chips"])}</td></tr>')
    raw(f'<table class="op-acc"><thead><tr><th>Model</th><th>Typical error</th><th>Inside 80% range</th><th>{NOUN[kind]}</th></tr></thead>'
        f"<tbody>{rows}</tbody></table>")
```

```{python}
LABELS = {
    "processor": "Chip", "class": "Classification", "measured": "Measured",
    "pred_ols": "OLS predicted", "residual_pct": "OLS %",
    "pred_structural": "Structural predicted", "structural_residual_pct": "Structural %",
    "pred_nonlinear": "Nonlinear predicted", "gbdt_residual_pct": "Nonlinear %",
    "model_spread_pts": "Model spread (pts)", "outside_training_range": "Outside training range",
    "tuning_spread_pct": "Config spread (pts)", "peak_gain_pct": "Peak vs base gain %",
    "workload_specialization_pct": "Workload specialization %",
    "n_results": "Disclosures", "n_oems": "OEMs", "n_systems": "Systems", "n_configs": "Configurations",
    "cores_per_chip": "Cores/chip", "l3_mb_per_core": "L3 MB/core", "score_per_core": "Score/core",
    "first_avail": "First available", "compiler_family": "Compiler",
    "first_test_date": "First test", "last_test_date": "Last test",
    "config_memory": "Memory tested", "config_system": "System", "Disclosure": "Disclosure",
    "vram_gb": "VRAM GB", "bandwidth_gbps": "Bandwidth GB/s", "form_factor": "Form factor",
    "suites_tested": "Suites",
}


def ranking(kind):
    df = DATA[kind]
    table = df.assign(
        **{"class": df["cls"].map(lambda c: CLASSES[c][0]),
           "measured": df["measured_per_socket" if kind == "cpu" else "measured_score"],
           "Disclosure": [f'<a href="{u}">report</a>' if u else "" for u in df["disclosure_url"]]}
    )
    cols = ["processor", "class", "measured", "pred_ols", "residual_pct", "pred_structural",
            "structural_residual_pct", "pred_nonlinear", "gbdt_residual_pct", "model_spread_pts",
            "outside_training_range", "tuning_spread_pct"]
    if kind == "cpu":
        cols += ["peak_gain_pct", "n_results", "n_oems", "n_systems", "n_configs", "cores_per_chip",
                 "l3_mb_per_core", "score_per_core", "compiler_family", "first_avail", "first_test_date",
                 "last_test_date", "config_memory", "Disclosure"]
    else:
        cols += ["workload_specialization_pct", "n_results", "n_oems", "n_systems", "n_configs",
                 "cores_per_chip", "vram_gb", "bandwidth_gbps", "form_factor", "suites_tested",
                 "first_avail", "config_system", "Disclosure"]
    table = table[cols].rename(columns=LABELS)
    if kind == "gpu":
        table = table.rename(columns={"Cores/chip": "Shaders", "First available": "Released"})
    show(table.round(1), paging=True, pageLength=25, order=[[4, "desc"]], showIndex=False,
         classes="display compact", allow_html=True, lengthMenu=[25, 100, 1000])


def breakdown(kind):
    g = group_table(kind).rename(columns={
        "compiler_family": "Compiler" if kind == "cpu" else "Suite", "chips": NOUN[kind],
        "disclosures": "Disclosures", "spread": "Median config spread (pts)",
        "configs": "Median configurations per chip", "ols": "Median OLS %", "nonlinear": "Median nonlinear %",
    })
    show(g.round(1), paging=False, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")


def validation(kind):
    v = VAL[kind]
    if v.empty:
        display(Markdown("Validation has not been exported yet."))
        return
    t = v.rename(columns={"slice": "Slice", "group": "Group", "model": "Model", "n_chips": NOUN[kind],
                          "median_abs_pct_error": "Typical error %", "mean_abs_log_error": "Mean abs log error",
                          "range_coverage_pct": "Inside 80% range %"})
    show(t.round(3), paging=True, pageLength=25, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")


def summary(title, note):
    print(f"<summary><b>{title}</b><span>{note}</span>{icon('chev', 'op-chev')}</summary>")
```

```{python}
    )[["Kind", "name", "coverage_status", "reason", "spec_results", "spec_oems", "Value", "Fair", "Here",
       "price_usd", "price_date", "blender_score", "benchmarks_collected"]].rename(columns={

        "price_usd": "Price (USD)", "price_date": "Price date", "blender_score": "Blender score",
        "benchmarks_collected": "SPEC collected",
    })
```

**Measured**: ranked here, with at least four results from more than one OEM. **Limited
evidence**: ranked on fewer results or a single OEM, or below the minimum number of results.
**Missing specifications**: SPEC results exist but the card is not in the specification table.
**Parsing failure**: a SPEC row names the product but no score could be read. **Results not
found**: no SPEC result in the collected suites, either because none is published (missing
measurements) or because the source does not cover that kind of product (SPEC GWPG is
workstation submissions, so consumer graphics cards rarely appear). Products on Value ranking or
Fair price are listed first. CPU specifications come from the SPEC disclosures; GPU specifications
come from the table in `pdi/tech_value/gwpg.py`.
:::
</details>

**Config spread** is the gap, in percentage points, between a chip's highest and lowest OLS
residual across its submitted results. It measures how much the submitted configurations
(system, memory, compiler, operating system, or for GPUs the workstation and suite) move the
score. It is not a tuning gain. Two other measurements are kept separate: the CPU **peak versus
base compiler gain** (SPEC's peak run against its base run on the same system) and the GPU
**workload specialization** (best single workload against the composite).
:::

Each chip contributes one median residual. The **baseline** predicts score from cores (or
shaders) times clock with one fitted constant. A model that does not beat it in a group adds
little there.
:::

<details class="op-detail">
```{python}
#| output: asis
summary("Models, definitions &amp; limitations", "OLS · Structural L1 · Nonlinear GBDT · provenance")
```
::: {.op-detail-body}

**Held out by chip.** Every chip is scored by models refitted without any of its results.
For CPUs, single-socket "P" parts (such as EPYC 9454P) are held out together with the part of
the same silicon (EPYC 9454), so a near-identical chip cannot help predict it. A chip's residual
is the median over its results of how far the measured score is above (positive) or below
(negative) the prediction. CPUs need at least `{python} cpu_meta.get("min_results", 3)` results
to be ranked, GPUs at least `{python} gpu_meta.get("min_results", 2)`.

**Scores.** CPU scores are SPECrate 2017 Integer base per socket, the median over a processor's
results, because SPECrate grows with the number of sockets. GPU scores combine several SPEC GWPG
suites and resolutions. Each suite and resolution is put on the SPECviewperf 2020 v3 scale
before fitting, so a GPU score is this site's estimate, not a SPEC metric. A documented
calibration check for that step is planned.

**The three models.**

* **OLS** is a plain regression in logs on cores, clock, chips, SMT, L2 and L3 cache per core,
  vintage and vendor (for GPUs: shaders, boost clock, VRAM, memory bandwidth, mobile form factor
  and vendor).
* **Structural L1** is a robust regression that lets returns to core or shader count diminish,
  with cache-by-density and bandwidth interactions.
* **Nonlinear GBDT** is a gradient-boosted tree model with median loss over the same
  specifications.

**Ranges and flags.** A chip's 80% range is its predicted score widened by the 10th and 90th
percentiles of every other chip's residual for that model. **Model spread** is the gap between
the highest and lowest of the three residuals. **Outside training range** names any
specification on which the chip is beyond every other chip, where predictions extrapolate.
**Limited evidence** marks a chip with fewer than four results, or with every result from one
OEM.

**Classes.** *Above prediction across models*: above all three predictions (CPUs: OLS +10% or
more, structural and nonlinear +8% or more, and OLS and nonlinear within 25 points).
*Below prediction across models*: below all three (CPUs: −10%, −8%, −8%), a candidate for
checking scaling, configuration or model limits. *Model-sensitive*: high on the straight-line OLS
but much smaller once nonlinear scaling is allowed for. Everything else is *near prediction*.
GPU thresholds are similar.

```{python}
#| output: asis
v = cpu_meta.get("verdict") or {}
if v:
    print(f"**Does the CPU model carry signal at all?** {v['statement']} See "
          "[Model and leaderboard](model.qmd).\n")
```

**Provenance.** Benchmarks: SPEC CPU 2017 collected `{python} collected(cpu_meta)`, SPEC GWPG
collected `{python} collected(gpu_meta)`. CPU specifications come from each SPEC disclosure.
GPU specifications come from a table kept in this repository. Prices, where shown, are the dated
lowest new listing used on Value ranking and Fair price; most SPEC-tested chips have none. Every
row links to its SPEC disclosure where SPEC publishes one.

**Limitations.** A residual flags unexplained performance; it is not a quality score.
Architecture, memory configuration, compiler, BIOS settings and model fit all contribute, and
vendors choose which configurations to submit. The spread and scaling charts describe the
submitted results and do not separate these causes.

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const MODELS = { ols: "OLS", structural: "Structural L1", nonlinear: "Nonlinear GBDT" };
  const signed = v => `${v > 0 ? "+" : v < 0 ? "−" : ""}${Math.abs(v).toFixed(1)}%`;
  const num = v => v == null ? "—" : v.toLocaleString("en-US", { maximumFractionDigits: v < 100 ? 1 : 0 });
  const esc = s => String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;" }[c]));
  const mainGraph = cat => cat.querySelector(".op-main .js-plotly-plot");
  document.querySelectorAll(".op-cat").forEach(cat => {
    const pick = cat.querySelector(".op-pick");
    if (!pick) return;
    const chips = JSON.parse(pick.dataset.chips);
    const select = pick.querySelector("select");
    const field = f => pick.querySelector(`[data-f="${f}"]`);
    const kind = cat.dataset.kind;
    const noun = kind === "cpu" ? "CPUs" : "GPUs";
    cat._opModel = "ols";
    // A product picked on another Tech Value page, or in a shared link, replaces the default.
    const shared = chips.find(d => d.key === window.TVPick?.get(kind));
    if (shared) select.value = shared.name;

    // Peer filters: narrow the main chart to comparable chips and say where the pick sits.
    const bar = cat.querySelector(".op-peers");
    const pv = n => bar?.querySelector(`[data-peer="${n}"]`)?.value ?? "";
    const pn = n => { const v = pv(n); return v === "" ? null : Number(v); };
    let peerSet = null;
    const peerCount = () => {
      if (!bar) return;
      const ok = peerSet ? chips.filter(c => peerSet.has(c.name)) : chips;
      const m = cat._opModel;
      const res = ok.map(c => c.preds[m].r).sort((a, b) => a - b);
      const mid = res.length ? (res[Math.floor((res.length - 1) / 2)] + res[Math.ceil((res.length - 1) / 2)]) / 2 : null;
      const sel = chips.find(d => d.name === select.value);
      let txt = `${ok.length} of ${chips.length} ${noun} comparable`;
      if (mid != null) txt += ` · median residual vs ${MODELS[m]} ${signed(mid)}`;
      if (sel && ok.includes(sel)) txt += ` · ${sel.name} ranks ${1 + ok.filter(c => c.preds[m].r > sel.preds[m].r).length} of ${ok.length} by residual`;
      else if (sel) txt += ` · ${sel.name} is outside these filters`;
      if (pn("p0") != null || pn("p1") != null) txt += " · price filters keep only chips with a retail price";
      bar.querySelector(".op-peer-count").textContent = txt;
    };
    const applyPeers = () => {
      if (!bar) return;
      const f = { vendor: pv("vendor"), group: pv("group"), form: pv("form"), g0: pn("gen0"), g1: pn("gen1"),
                  c0: pn("c0"), c1: pn("c1"), p0: pn("p0"), p1: pn("p1") };
      const priced = f.p0 != null || f.p1 != null;
      const ok = chips.filter(c => (!f.vendor || c.vendor === f.vendor) && (!f.group || c.group === f.group)
        && (!f.form || c.form === f.form)
        && (c.gen == null || ((f.g0 == null || c.gen >= f.g0) && (f.g1 == null || c.gen <= f.g1)))
        && (f.c0 == null || c.cores >= f.c0) && (f.c1 == null || c.cores <= f.c1)
        && (!priced || (c.price != null && (f.p0 == null || c.price >= f.p0) && (f.p1 == null || c.price <= f.p1))));
      peerSet = new Set(ok.map(c => c.name));
      const g = mainGraph(cat);
      if (g && window.Plotly) {
        const idx = [], xs = [], ys = [], cds = [];
        g.data.forEach((t, i) => {
          if (!t.name?.startsWith("m:")) return;
          if (!t._opAll) t._opAll = { x: Array.from(t.x), y: Array.from(t.y), c: Array.from(t.customdata) };
          const keep = t._opAll.c.map(cd => peerSet.has(cd[0]));
          idx.push(i);
          xs.push(t._opAll.x.filter((_, j) => keep[j]));
          ys.push(t._opAll.y.filter((_, j) => keep[j]));
          cds.push(t._opAll.c.filter((_, j) => keep[j]));
        });
        if (idx.length) Plotly.restyle(g, { x: xs, y: ys, customdata: cds }, idx);
      }
      peerCount();
    };
    if (bar) {
      bar.addEventListener("change", applyPeers);
      bar.addEventListener("input", e => { if (e.target.tagName === "INPUT") applyPeers(); });
      bar.querySelector('[data-peer="reset"]').addEventListener("click", () => {
        bar.querySelectorAll("input").forEach(i => { i.value = ""; });
        bar.querySelectorAll("select").forEach(s => {
          s.selectedIndex = s.dataset.peer === "gen1" ? s.options.length - 1 : 0;
        });
        applyPeers();
      });
    }

    const update = () => {
      const c = chips.find(d => d.name === select.value) || chips[0];
      window.TVPick?.render(kind, c.key);
      peerCount();
      field("name").textContent = c.name;
      field("cls").textContent = c.cls;
      let rows = `<tr class="op-measured"><td>Measured</td><td>${num(c.y)}</td><td></td><td></td></tr>`;
      for (const [k, label] of Object.entries(MODELS)) {
        const p = c.preds[k];
        const range = p.lo == null ? "—" : `${num(p.lo)} – ${num(p.hi)}`;
        rows += `<tr><td>${label}</td><td>${num(p.p)}</td><td>${range}</td><td class="${p.r >= 0 ? "op-pos" : "op-negv"}">${signed(p.r)}</td></tr>`;
      }
      field("preds").innerHTML = rows;
      const flags = [`Model spread ${c.spread.toFixed(1)} pts`];
      if (c.oor) flags.push(`Outside training range: ${c.oor}`);
      if (c.limited) flags.push("Limited evidence: few results or one OEM");
      field("flags").innerHTML = (c.oor || c.limited ? `<svg class="op-ico" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 3l10 18H2z"/><path d="M12 10v5M12 18v.5"/></svg> ` : "") + esc(flags.join(" · "));
      field("flags").style.color = c.oor || c.limited ? "" : "var(--op-muted)";
      field("facts").innerHTML = c.facts.map(([k, v]) => `<div><span>${esc(k)}</span><b>${esc(v)}</b></div>`).join("");
      field("link").innerHTML = c.url ? `<a href="${esc(c.url)}">Typical SPEC disclosure</a>` : "";
      const g = mainGraph(cat);
      if (!g || !window.Plotly) return;
      const idx = g.data.findIndex(t => t.name === "selected");
      if (idx >= 0) Plotly.restyle(g, { x: [[c.preds[cat._opModel].p]], y: [[c.y]] }, [idx]);
    };
    select.addEventListener("change", () => {
      const c = chips.find(d => d.name === select.value);
      if (c) window.TVPick?.set(kind, c.key);
      update();
    });
    cat._opUpdate = update;
    const g = mainGraph(cat);
    if (g?.on) g.on("plotly_click", ev => {
      const name = ev.points?.[0]?.customdata?.[0];
      if (name && [...select.options].some(o => o.text === name)) { select.value = name; select.dispatchEvent(new Event("change")); }
    });
    cat.querySelectorAll("button[data-model]").forEach(btn => btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const m = btn.dataset.model;
      cat._opModel = m;
      cat.querySelectorAll("button[data-model]").forEach(b => b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(b === btn)));
      const graph = mainGraph(cat);
      if (graph && window.Plotly) {
        const idx = [], vis = [];
        graph.data.forEach((t, i) => { if (t.name?.startsWith("m:")) { idx.push(i); vis.push(t.name.startsWith(`m:${m}:`)); } });
        Plotly.restyle(graph, { visible: vis }, idx);
        Plotly.relayout(graph, { "xaxis.title.text": `Predicted by ${MODELS[m]} (log scale)` });
      }
      update();
    }));
    cat.querySelectorAll("button[data-alt]").forEach(btn => btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const card = btn.closest(".op-card");
      card.querySelectorAll("button[data-alt]").forEach(b => b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(b === btn)));
      card.querySelectorAll(".op-alt").forEach(d => { d.hidden = d.dataset.alt !== btn.dataset.alt; });
      card.querySelectorAll(".op-alt:not([hidden]) .js-plotly-plot").forEach(gr => { if (window.Plotly) { Plotly.Plots.resize(gr); fitPhone(gr); } });
    }));
  });
  // Phone width: thin the tick labels and shorten axis titles so nothing is clipped.
  function fitPhone(g) {
    if (!g || !window.Plotly || g._opPhone || g.offsetWidth === 0 || g.offsetWidth >= 600) return;
    g._opPhone = true;
    const upd = { "margin.l": Math.min(g.layout.margin.l, 56) };
    for (const ax of ["xaxis", "yaxis"]) {
      const a = g.layout[ax], t = a.title?.text || "";
      if (t.startsWith("Measured:")) upd[`${ax}.title.text`] = "Measured";
      else if (t.length > 30) upd[`${ax}.title.text`] = t.replace(" (log scale)", "").replace("Median spread across submitted configurations", "Median spread");
      if (a.tickvals && a.ticktext && a.tickvals.length > 7) {
        upd[`${ax}.tickvals`] = a.tickvals.filter((_, i) => i % 2 === 0);
        upd[`${ax}.ticktext`] = a.ticktext.filter((_, i) => i % 2 === 0);
      }
    }
    Plotly.relayout(g, upd);
  }
  const show = kind => {
    document.body.classList.toggle("op-gpu", kind === "gpu");
    document.querySelectorAll(".op-toggle button").forEach(b => b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(b.dataset.tab === kind)));
    document.querySelectorAll(`.op-cat[data-kind="${kind}"]`).forEach(cat => {
      cat.querySelectorAll(".js-plotly-plot").forEach(g => { if (window.Plotly && g.offsetWidth) { Plotly.Plots.resize(g); fitPhone(g); } });
      cat._opUpdate?.();
    });
  };
  document.querySelectorAll(".op-toggle button").forEach(b => b.addEventListener("click", () => {
    show(b.dataset.tab);
    try { history.replaceState(null, "", b.dataset.tab === "gpu" ? "#gpu" : location.pathname + location.search); } catch (e) {}
  }));
  show(location.hash === "#gpu" || window.TVPick?.urlKind() === "gpu" ? "gpu" : "cpu");

  // Two-product comparison from the shared catalogue.
  const usd = v => "$" + Math.round(v).toLocaleString("en-US");
  const diff = (a, b) => (a && b ? signed(100 * (b / a - 1)) : "");
  document.querySelectorAll(".op-cmp").forEach(box => {
    if (!window.TVPick) return;
    const kind = box.dataset.kind;
    const ia = box.querySelector('[data-cmp="a"]');
    const ib = box.querySelector('[data-cmp="b"]');
    const body = box.querySelector('[data-cmp="body"]');
    const sum = box.querySelector('[data-cmp="sum"]');
    TVPick.load().then(all => {
      const mine = all.filter(r => r.kind === kind);
      if (!mine.length) { body.innerHTML = "<tr><td>The catalogue could not be loaded.</td></tr>"; return; }
      const byKey = k => mine.find(r => r.model_key === k);
      const byName = n => mine.find(r => r.name === n);
      const first = byKey(TVPick.get(kind)) || byKey(box.dataset.a) || mine[0];
      let second = byKey(box.dataset.b) || mine[1];
      if (second === first) second = byKey(box.dataset.a) || mine.find(r => r !== first);
      ia.value = first.name;
      ib.value = second.name;
      const spec = r => r.spec_score != null ? num(r.spec_score) : (r.spec_results ? "Not ranked" : "No SPEC result");
      const rank = r => r.value_rank ? `#${r.value_rank} of ${r.value_n}` : "Not ranked";
      const verdict = r => r.on_residuals ? `${r.consensus_verdict || "Near prediction"} <small>${signed(r.residual_pct)} vs OLS</small>` : `Not ranked <small>${esc(r.reason || "")}</small>`;
      const draw = () => {
        const a = byName(ia.value), b = byName(ib.value);
        if (!a || !b) { sum.textContent = "Pick two products from the list."; return; }
        const rowsHtml = [
          ["Coverage", r => `${esc(r.coverage_status)}${r.reason ? `<small>${esc(r.reason)}</small>` : ""}`, null],
          ["Retail price", r => r.price_usd != null ? `${usd(r.price_usd)}<small>${esc(r.price_date || "")}</small>` : "No current price", "price_usd"],
          ["Blender score", r => r.blender_score != null ? num(r.blender_score) : "No Blender result", "blender_score"],
          ["Blender points per dollar", r => r.score_per_dollar != null ? r.score_per_dollar.toFixed(2) : "—", "score_per_dollar"],
          ["Value ranking", rank, null],
          ["Fair price estimate", r => r.fair_price_usd != null ? `${usd(r.fair_price_usd)}<small>listing ${signed(r.fair_gap_pct)} vs estimate</small>` : "No estimate", null],
          [kind === "cpu" ? "SPEC score per socket" : "Calibrated SPEC GWPG score", spec, "spec_score"],
          ["Against prediction", verdict, null],
          ["SPEC evidence", r => `${r.spec_results} results · ${r.spec_oems} OEM${r.spec_oems === 1 ? "" : "s"}`, null],
        ].map(([label, f, col]) => `<tr><td>${label}</td><td>${f(a)}</td><td>${f(b)}</td><td>${col ? diff(a[col], b[col]) : ""}</td></tr>`).join("");
        body.innerHTML = `<tr><th></th><th>${esc(a.name)}</th><th>${esc(b.name)}</th><th>Second vs first</th></tr>` + rowsHtml;
        const parts = [];
        if (a.blender_score && b.blender_score && a.price_usd && b.price_usd) {
          const s = 100 * (b.blender_score / a.blender_score - 1), p = 100 * (b.price_usd / a.price_usd - 1);
          const v = 100 * (b.score_per_dollar / a.score_per_dollar - 1);
          parts.push(`${esc(b.name)} scores ${Math.abs(s).toFixed(0)}% ${s >= 0 ? "higher" : "lower"} in Blender at ${Math.abs(p).toFixed(0)}% ${p >= 0 ? "more" : "less"} money, so it gives ${Math.abs(v).toFixed(0)}% ${v >= 0 ? "more" : "fewer"} Blender points per dollar.`);
        }
        if (a.spec_score != null && b.spec_score != null) {
          const d = 100 * (b.spec_score / a.spec_score - 1);
          parts.push(`On SPEC it measures ${Math.abs(d).toFixed(0)}% ${d >= 0 ? "higher" : "lower"}.`);
        } else if (a.spec_score != null || b.spec_score != null) {
          parts.push(`Only ${esc((a.spec_score != null ? a : b).name)} has a ranked SPEC result, so SPEC can't compare the two.`);
        }
        sum.innerHTML = parts.join(" ");
      };
      ia.addEventListener("change", draw);
      ib.addEventListener("change", draw);
      draw();
    });
  });
  const settle = () => show(document.body.classList.contains("op-gpu") ? "gpu" : "cpu");
  setTimeout(settle, 300);
  window.addEventListener("load", settle);
});
</script>
